headline: Strong wind and steady rain tonight into Sunday, then drier weather midweek.
summary: A cold front from the Pacific is bringing strong wind and steady rain tonight into Sunday. Behind it, a dip in the high-altitude winds, called an upper-level trough, keeps showers possible through Monday, mostly in the Olympics and Cascades. Midweek, a deep low-pressure system is expected to track toward northern California, steering most of its rain south of us for a drier spell. Forecasters are less sure how close it gets, and wetter weather may return next weekend. Gusts of 50 to 55 mph are likely on the coast and in the San Juans, with high surf there and a flood watch for the Skokomish River.
changes: Compared with this morning, the midweek system is now described as a deep low tracking toward northern California, and forecasters are a bit less sure how close it comes. Wind gust forecasts also edged up to 50 to 55 mph.
